metadata.note: The European and North American Railway through Danforth — Bangor to Vanceboro on the New Brunswick border, conceived by John A. Poor to join the US rail network to an ice-free Atlantic port. Completed over its 114 miles in October 1871, leased by the Maine Central in 1882 as its Eastern Division main line, and from 1889 also carrying Canadian Pacific's Montreal-Saint John trains on trackage rights, which CP converted to outright ownership in 1974. Maine Central's own passenger service ended in 1960, but Danforth kept its trains far longer than that: VIA Rail's Atlantic still set down Maine passengers there until it was discontinued on Dec 17 1994.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_and_North_American_Railway (Bangor to Olamon opened 1868, Olamon to Mattawamkeag 1869, and the 114-mile line completed to Vanceboro in October 1871, linking to the E&NA Western Extension at Vanceboro-St. Croix)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Pacific_Lines_in_Maine (from 1889 to 1974 CP's Montreal-Saint John through route used trackage rights over the Maine Central between Mattawamkeag and Vanceboro; CP purchased the line outright from the MEC in 1974; CP formed the Canadian Atlantic Railway in 1988 and sold the remaining assets in December 1994)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_(train) (the route ran through Maine until 1994; in the Atlantic's last incarnation, 1985-94, most cars were sealed but one coach door allowed Maine passengers to board or detrain at Jackman, Greenville, Brownville Junction, Mattawamkeag, Danforth and Vanceboro; VIA discontinued the Atlantic on Dec 17 1994; the line was sold in sections on Jan 1 1995, the border-to-Mattawamkeag-to-Brownville Junction portion going to the Eastern Maine Railway)
Maine Central ran its last passenger train in 1960 and became freight-only -- from secondary summaries of Maine Central passenger service, not checked against a timetable
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways are estimates throughout and no timetable has been consulted. The 1978 boundary between the Canadian Pacific and VIA Rail features is the year VIA took over Canada's intercity passenger services generally, not a documented change on this route. Maine Central's 1960 end is a year, not a dated last train, and whether Danforth kept a local MEC stop right to the end is not established. The Bangor-Mattawamkeag portion is drawn for the E&NA and Maine Central features but NOT for the CP and VIA features, because those trains came from Montreal via Brownville Junction rather than from Bangor -- their approach west of Mattawamkeag is not drawn at all.

segments.note: John A. Poor's scheme to link the US rail network with an ice-free Atlantic port. Construction reached Olamon in 1868 and Mattawamkeag in 1869, and the 114-mile line was completed to Vanceboro in October 1871, meeting the New Brunswick E&NA at the St. Croix. Danforth's station dates from 1871. Frequency estimated/unsourced

segments.note: Maine Central leased the E&NA between Bangor and Vanceboro in 1882 and ran it as its Eastern Division main line. A photograph of the Danforth station survives from 1923, when the town's population was heading for its 1930 peak of about 1,467. Maine Central ran its last passenger train in 1960 and became a freight-only railroad; the Canadian Pacific bought this line outright from MEC in 1974. Frequency estimated/unsourced

segments.note: From 1889 the Canadian Pacific ran its Montreal-Saint John trains over this stretch on trackage rights from the Maine Central, the final link in CP's route to an ice-free Atlantic port. It bought the line outright in 1974. So Danforth sat on a Canadian transcontinental connection as well as a Maine local line. Frequency estimated/unsourced

segments.note: VIA Rail took over Canada's intercity passenger services and ran the Atlantic, Montreal to Halifax by way of Maine and Saint John. In its last form, 1985-94, most cars were sealed through the United States but one coach door stayed open so Maine passengers could board or alight at Jackman, Greenville, Brownville Junction, Mattawamkeag, DANFORTH and Vanceboro. VIA discontinued the Atlantic on Dec 17 1994, because a pending change of ownership would have put its trains on track owned by neither Canadian national railway. The line was sold off in sections on Jan 1 1995. Frequency estimated/unsourced
